title: How GPT-3 responds to different publics on climate change and Black Lives Matter: A critical appraisal of equity in conversational AI

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing user experience, learning outcomes, and GPT-3's response styles (using Structural Topic Modeling and Linguistic Inquiry and Word Count sentiment analysis) between users holding majority versus minority opinions on climate change and the Black Lives Matter movement.

Evaluating differences in user experience, knowledge gain, and chatbot conversational styles (e.g., use of justifications and negative expressions) when interacting with users who have a bachelor's degree or higher compared to those with lower educational attainment.

Analyzing human-AI dialogues and post-chat survey ratings using OLS regressions to measure differences in user experience, topic prevalence, and sentiment in GPT-3's responses between white and non-white participants.
Measuring disparities in chatbot user experience and response linguistic features between participants whose first language is English versus non-native English speakers.
Testing for significant divides in user experience and conversational equity between male and female participants through regression analysis of post-dialogue survey results.
